title: Known limitations
note: Headings are read from the documents at build time, never retyped, so an entry that is resolved there cannot stay open here. Resolved means fixed; closed means the entry reached a terminal state without a fix, and the two are counted separately.

entries.title: Flat confidence under duplication depends on training-time adaptation
Residual per-pair dependence accumulates with view count
The discount addresses redundant evidence, not unreliable evidence
The discount is proportional, not capping, and weakens as evidence grows
The suspicion detector inherits the dependence signal's blind spot, and inverts under missing evidence
The shared/private objective does not fix which branch carries cross-view information, and ENIV reads only one of them
Tail dependence is not the sharper instrument the argument predicted; it inverts under strong attack
Detection and correction fail together, because both read cross-view belief agreement
ENIV is validated only on synthetic data, where rho is a parameter we set
Dependence is estimated from finite batches, and the estimator is biased
Tail dependence is unreliable below 50 exceedances, and the threshold bites
The attacker capabilities that defeat the defence are specific, and only partly tested
V1 detaches the discount, so it corrects inference but never shapes representation
One dataset family, and five seeds that are five partitions of it
No human-subject evaluation and no deployment evaluation were run
On real cross-scenario data, discrimination and calibration come apart, and the positive class is one or three episodes
On AIT the label is solved by one view, so Part 28 is not evidence about fusion
On real data the detector inverts under attack, and the protocol cannot speak to deployment
The coordination term's effect depends on the view and the direction
Part 09's L3 extension is only partially reproduced on AIT
Fixed epsilon is not comparable across views or directions
Part 10's clone comparison is not like-for-like
CLOSED 2026-10-26, confirmed not lifted. On LANL the reported prevalence is a declared case-control sample, not the network
On LANL the `auth` view is label-adjacent, and dropping it does not drop the selection
Part 28's scaler and trainer are not reusable across datasets
CLOSED 2026-10-26, confirmed not lifted. On LANL the models' advantage over a trivial scalar is confined to seen attack computers
On LANL one host carries a third of the attack class, with no benign contrast
On LANL the execution mode changes the fitted weights, and the per-seed std understates the spread
CLOSED 2026-10-26, diagnosed not fixed. On two LANL arms the probabilities are worse than a constant
What Part 30 does not establish
One window length per real dataset, and no sensitivity analysis
Part 32's container image has never been built
